text: Nathan has recently qualified as an accountant. His neighbour, Maureen, invites Nathan to a party.
At the party, she tells him that she has inherited a large amount of money and is thinking about
using it to buy and run the café which is located on the high street. Maureen shows Nathan a copy
of the most recent set of accounts for the café. Nathan looks through the accounts quickly and
tells Maureen that it appears that the café is profitable. Maureen buys the café.
After six months, the café is yet to make a profit. She consults a business advisor who tells her
that in fact the accounts show that the café has not made a profit for several years. Maureen is
forced to close the café at a significant financial loss.
Having lost her inheritance on the café, Maureen is very angry with Nathan. One evening Maureen
is walking outside and sees Nathan. She stands in his way, telling him that he cannot pass until he
admits fault for her financial loss. Nathan moves towards her, shouting ‘get out of the way or I will
make you move’. Maureen refuses to move and Nathan pushes her. Maureen falls and breaks her
wrist.
Advise the parties of their rights, responsibilities and potential remedies. [25]
OR
Barchester University wants to encourage its students to walk to their lectures to reduce the level
of pollution associated with driving. The university has created pedestrian-only pathways on its
campus so that students can walk from their accommodation to the lecture halls. The university
has put up signs stating ‘no cycling’, but it has received a number of complaints about cyclists
using the pathways.
Clive, a cyclist, is using the pathway and as he is late for his lecture he is cycling very quickly.
His bicycle slips on the uneven surface, and he falls to the ground. He breaks his arm, and his
expensive bicycle is damaged beyond repair.
Following this incident, the university authorities prohibit the use of the pathways. New signs
stating that the pathways are not in use are placed around the campus. Jim and Eoin continue
to use the pathways to walk to lectures. On one occasion a security guard tells them to leave the
pathway and they do. As a joke Jim pushes Eoin back on to the pathway. The security guard tells
Eoin to leave the pathway but he refuses and continues to walk.
Advise the parties of their rights, responsibilities and potential remedies. [25]
Section B
Answer two questions from this section.
To ensure a fair outcome, special considerations must apply to the defence of contributory
negligence when the claimant is a child.
Assess the validity of the statement above. [25]
The rules which determine who can sue or be sued for a private nuisance are unnecessarily strict.
Assess the validity of the statement above. [25]
The reasonable man test ensures a consistent approach to breach of duty in negligence.
Assess the validity of the statement above. [25]
